prompt:
Hydrogen reacts with oxygen to form water:

$2\text{H}_2+\text{O}_2\rightarrow2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

If $8.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2$ reacts completely with excess oxygen, what mass of water is produced? Use $M(\text{H}_2)=2.0\text{ g/mol}$ and $M(\text{H}_2\text{O})=18.0\text{ g/mol}$.
teacher_notes: Students who skip the mole ratio and scale by mass alone report 72 g by luck here; ask them to redo it with the oxygen mass to expose the shortcut.
explanation: Convert to moles: $n(\text{H}_2)=\frac{8.0\text{ g}}{2.0\text{ g/mol}}=4.0\text{ mol}$. The balanced equation gives a $2:2$, or $1:1$, mole ratio of $\text{H}_2$ to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so $4.0\text{ mol}$ of water forms. Convert back to mass: $m=(4.0\text{ mol})(18.0\text{ g/mol})=72\text{ g}$.
